Jeff used phoropter all morning on a .NET course repository, with another Claude, and that Claude kept notes for phoropter as it went. It's the first time a repository that isn't phoropter or mock-control has gone from draft to as-built. Most of it worked. What didn't is small, but each one cost a detour or would mislead the next reader. This plan takes the notes that are ready.

One note changes the format, and gets its own draft next: how evidence that arrives after an as-built freezes answers an older guess. The note about whether Decision, Decline and Guess suit teaching decisions waits for a plan or two in that repository.

Decision: The dev server follows HEAD

where scip-go gomod github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter . `github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter/internal/site`/Serve(). symbol page

quote h := &handler{site: s, root: o.Out, repoDir: o.Repo.Dir}

Because (the course repo's notes, measured, then Claude and Jeff): the server builds once, at the commit where it started. Six commits later, the home page still said "at 6018106", and the draft page showed a generated commit older than the draft's own base:. That reads backwards, and a reader could take it to mean the repository hasn't moved. It's usually the agent that starts the server, in the background, so nobody's there to restart it.

On a request, when --at is HEAD (the default) and HEAD has moved, the server builds the new commit into a fresh directory, then swaps it in, so no request sees half a site. It prints a line saying so, and updates the commit in its serving file. A server started at another commit stays there, since that's what was asked for. HEAD is checked on a request, at most once a second (Claude, and Jeff agreed): git rev-parse costs a few milliseconds, and a file watcher would rebuild for commits nobody looks at and needs another dependency.

Decision: A key menu when the server runs in a terminal, as Vite has

where scip-go gomod github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter . `github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter`/main(). symbol page

quote signal.Notify(stop, syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)

Because (Jeff): a person running phoropter should be able to restart it or get back to it without remembering commands. After the serving line, it prints press h + enter to show help, as Vite does. The keys:

  • r: rebuild now, at HEAD
  • o: open the site in the browser
  • u: print the address again
  • q: quit
  • h: list these

Each key is followed by enter, as Vite does (Jeff chose it): keys alone need the terminal in raw mode, which changes how every line of the server's output prints and has to be undone on every way out, including a crash. The menu only appears when stdin is a terminal. Run in the background, by an agent, nothing reads stdin and nothing changes.

Decline: Opening the TUI from the server's menu

Because (Claude, not asked): a t key that runs phoropter ui in the same terminal and returns to the server log on quit is appealing. But the server and the TUI would share one terminal, and the server's log lines would land on top of the TUI. It waits until someone wants it enough to work that out.

Decision: "Nothing defined" says what phoropter can tell

where scip-go gomod github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter . `github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter`/symbols(). symbol page

quote fail(fmt.Sprintf("nothing defined in %s at %s (uncommitted changes aren't indexed)", rel, repo.Short(sha)))

Because (the course repo's notes, measured): the message blamed uncommitted changes in two cases where both files were clean. In one, the file lost to a copy with the same project name, elsewhere in the repository. In the other, it was a Program.cs of top-level statements, which has no names to anchor. The other Claude ran the indexer by hand to find out. Top-level Program.cs is how every new ASP.NET Core app starts, so C# users will see this often.

The message now says only what's true:

  • The file has uncommitted changes: say so, as now.
  • A file with the same path below some directory has definitions (…/Vendors/Api.cs and instructor/…/Vendors/Api.cs): name it, and say that copies with one package name are indexed at the first path. It works after copies diverge, which in a course repo they do as the session goes.
  • Otherwise: say the file has no named declarations, as with top-level statements, and that a file anchor with a quote reaches it.

Decision: The indexer guide says how a collapsed copy shows itself

where indexers/README.md file page

quote same symbol, the first in path order wins. Never number overloads or otherwise

Because (the course repo's notes, measured): the rule was right and the silence was the problem. A student's copy of Software.Api vanished from phoropter symbols, missing was empty, and nothing said why. The guide adds that phoropter symbols names the copy that won, so the reader writing a plan finds out at the moment it matters.

Decline: An indexer contract field for duplicate packages

Because (Claude, not asked): I suggested it first: the indexer would list the paths that lost. But phoropter can notice from what the indexer already prints, and the roslyn indexer lives in another repository, so changing the contract means changing it too. If the message above isn't enough, this is the next step.

Decline: Telling copies apart, or a .phoropter-ignore

Because (Jeff and Claude): Jeff raised an ignore file, and it would have handled the course repo: the student copy wasn't part of the story. Phoropter makes the checkout with git archive, so it could leave ignored paths out before indexing, read from each commit so older plans resolve as they did. But Jeff's previous course had fourteen lab starters, each with a Practice.AppHost, and there every copy is a story. Ignoring doesn't fit that. Telling copies apart might, but how is a design question with no repository to try it on. Jeff moved the student copy out, so neither is needed now.

Decision: phoropter indexers lists what this machine can index

where scip-go gomod github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter . `github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter`/usage. symbol page

quote phoropter symbols <file> [--scheme <scheme>]

Because (the course repo's notes, measured): nothing the other Claude read said how to get C# support on a new machine. indexers/ holds only Go and TypeScript, and the README names roslyn as an example. One line per indexer: its scheme, its extensions, its name and version, and where it was found (indexers/go, or a path on PATH). With none, it points at the README's indexer list. The organdy as-built's honest miss (a go installed binary finds no first-party indexers) shows up here too, plainly.

Decision: The guide's anchors start with what you do, not the grammar

where guide.md › Working with plans › 1. Write the plan › Anchors file page

quote Or a symbol, in SCIP's grammar, with the package version written as

Because (the course repo's notes, measured, then Jeff): the other Claude read the guide, saw "SCIP's grammar" and a scip-typescript example, and went looking for scip-dotnet. The workflow was in the middle of a sentence about schemes. Jeff's view: if a careful reader got it wrong, the guide should be clearer. The symbol bullet now says: run phoropter symbols <file> and paste a line; you never choose or type a scheme; phoropter indexers says which languages this machine indexes. The grammar is for people writing indexers, and indexers/README.md has it.

Decision: The guide's citations move to the end

where guide.md file page

quote This guide is the format, in the present tense. Each rule names the plan that decided it,

Because (the course repo's notes, then Jeff): on another repository's site, (lanyard) and (grommet) are names that mean nothing by design, mid-sentence, with nothing to click. The rules read fine without them. They keep their history in one closing section, "Where these rules came from", a line per rule. Jeff wanted them kept, since they show each rule has a reason, as long as the guide says plainly that they're history: plans in other repositories, mostly private, and nothing a reader needs to look up.

Decision: The guide says an answer can become its own decision

where guide.md › Working with plans › Drafts (optional) file page

quote (the date is today, the day you say "we're implementing this"), folds each answer into

Because (the course repo's notes): an answer declined a Question's premise and created new work, and "folds each answer into its entry's reason" didn't cover it. The other Claude made it a new Decision, which was right. One sentence says so.

Decision: The agent block says who runs the server, and the guide doesn't need one

where README.md › phoropter › Tell your agent file page

quote guide first: it's at `guide/` on the site (`phoropter url` prints the address), or

Because (Jeff): neither the guide nor the agent block says who starts the server. Jeff ran it this morning, but usually it'd be the agent. And Jeff saw the catch: the guide is a page on the server, so it can't be where the agent learns to start the server. Today the block says "read the guide at guide/ on the site", which needs a server that may not be running.

So the instructions live where the agent reads first, the block pasted into its CLAUDE.md: if phoropter url finds no server, start phoropter in the background and tell me the address. Following HEAD means one server lasts the session. And the guide stops depending on a server: it's already built into the binary, so phoropter guide prints it. The block says to read it that way.

Decision: A draft shows what's already at its places

where scip-go gomod github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter . `github.com/hypertheory-labs/phoropter/internal/site`/anchorHTML(). symbol page

quote place = fmt.Sprintf(` <a rel="anchored-at" itemprop="place" href="%s">%s page</a>`, Rel(here, ra.Place.Href), ra.Place.Kind)

Because (the course repo's notes, and the seed in shelf/draft-places.md): Jeff wants plans to catch a new one that confuses an old one. A draft is where that's cheapest, and today it only links each anchor to its place page. Now, under each draft anchor, the landed entries already there are listed, in the seed's order: guesses not yet answered (or answered not tested, since this work might be the test), then declines, then decisions. Each is a link with its kind and plan, as microdata, so the agent writing the draft reads it too. The TUI can show it later; until then the gaps ledger will list it. A conflict between ideas with no shared anchor still takes a reader.

Guess: Following HEAD costs nothing a reader notices

Answered in the as-built: disproved.

Disproved if: on phoropter's own repository, with its indexes in the store, the first request after a commit takes more than 3 seconds, or requests between commits get measurably slower.

Guess: The new message finds the copy that won in the course repo's shape

Answered in the as-built: held.

Disproved if: in a test with two copies of one package at different paths, diverged, phoropter symbols on the losing copy doesn't name the winning one.
